title: fix(comfy): use monotonic clock for workflow poll deadline
body:
## What Problem This Solves

ComfyUI image/video/music generation could hang past the configured workflow timeout or fail with a spurious timeout on healthy workflows when the system wall clock jumped (NTP skew, manual time change). The workflow poll deadline now uses a monotonic clock so wall-clock jumps cannot stretch or shrink the per-request timeout budget.

- Problem: `waitForComfyHistory` seeded its poll deadline with `Date.now()` and read the remaining budget with `Date.now()` too, but the remaining value is consumed by `setTimeout` (Node libuv monotonic timer) — a cross-clock-domain mismatch. A wall-clock rollback Δ inflated every per-request timeout and poll sleep by Δ (workflow hung past the configured `timeoutMs`); a forward jump Δ shrank the remaining budget to a negative value, prematurely failing healthy generation with "Comfy workflow did not finish within Ns".
- Solution: seed and read the deadline from `performance.now()` so the remaining budget stays on the same monotonic clock as the timer that consumes it.
- What changed: `extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts` — `waitForComfyHistory` deadline seed (L420) and `resolveComfyRemainingMs` remaining read (L482) switched from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`. `extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — the "caps oversized local workflow timeouts" test now spies on `performance.now` instead of `Date.now`, using an advancing `monotonicNow` value driven by the fetch mock so incidental `performance.now()` calls during provider init (plugin-metadata snapshot) cannot desync the seed/read sequence.
- What did NOT change: the error message format (`"Comfy workflow did not finish within Ns"`), poll loop logic, `timeoutMs` clamping via `resolvePositiveTimerTimeoutMs`, and all other `Date.now()` call sites in the file (used only for single-shot fixed timeouts, not remaining-budget arithmetic).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix lands in the canonical owner of the remaining-budget computation (`resolveComfyRemainingMs`) plus the single deadline seed site (`waitForComfyHistory`), so both consumption paths — `requestTimeoutMs` (→ `readJsonResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `setTimeout`) and `pollDelayMs` (→ `setTimeout`) — benefit from one change with no new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface. This matches the project convention stated by maintainers in #155648: "operation budgets use `performance.now()`, epoch timestamps stay `Date.now()`", and mirrors the canonical fix already merged in #155603 (BUG-081, codex remote-workspace-media) and the in-flight #155801 (BUG-085, codex attempt execution deadline).

- Best fix: yes — 2-line mechanical replacement at the canonical owner; no guard/branch added.
- Alternative considered: injecting a `now: () => number` parameter (like `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`) — rejected as over-engineering for a single internal call site with no persistence/cross-process concern (the deadline is a closure-local variable, never serialized or shared across processes).
- Risk: `performance.now()` returns a sub-millisecond float. The `requestTimeoutMs` path is floored downstream by `resolveSafeTimeoutDelayMs` (`src/utils/fetch-timeout.ts`); the `pollDelayMs` path feeds `setTimeout`, which accepts float delays. No `AbortSignal.timeout` integer-contract issue applies here (`buildTimeoutAbortSignal` uses `setTimeout`, not `AbortSignal.timeout`). Verified with `node --import tsx` direct invocation. steipete's open PR #117905 restructures this same region (introducing `ProviderOperationDeadline`); if it lands first this patch needs a rebase but is not a duplicate — #117905 still uses `Date.now()` for deadline comparison and does not address the cross-clock-domain issue.

## User Impact

Users generating media via ComfyUI (local or cloud mode) will no longer see intermittent hangs or spurious "did not finish within Ns" failures caused by wall-clock adjustments during long-running workflow polls. The configured `timeoutMs` now bounds the actual elapsed time regardless of NTP corrections or manual clock changes.

## Evidence

**Evidence at a glance** (for quick review):

| clock state | pre-fix (main, `Date.now()`) | post-fix (this PR, `performance.now()`) |
|---|---|---|
| wall forward +60s mid-poll | spurious timeout -- workflow fails to complete in 10s | completes in 809ms (bounded by real elapsed time) |
| wall rewind -60s, never-completing workflow | budget inflates -> still polling past **6017ms** (3x the 2000ms budget) | times out within configured 2000ms |
| wall rewind -60s, completing workflow | completes (inflated budget, no harm) | completes in 617ms (bounded) |
| normal (no skew) | completes normally | completes normally (same) |

**Pre-fix RED** -- 2 tests FAIL on main: `forward=spurious timeout` + `bounded-expiry=hang past budget (6017ms)`. Error: `expected true to be false # hitHardGuard: polling still alive at 3x the 2000ms budget`.

**Post-fix GREEN** -- all 3 scenarios PASS (forward jump bounded, backward jump bounded, normal completion intact).

Full proof details below.


Real behavior proof — production Comfy provider polling through a real HTTP client (real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `setTimeout`) against a live local `node:http` server, with `Date.now()` jumped ±60s mid-poll to simulate NTP skew / manual clock change. Three scenarios cover both failure modes: (A) forward jump causes a spurious timeout, (B) backward jump inflates the budget into a hang past the configured `timeoutMs`, (C) normal completion under both jump directions. Pre-fix uses `Date.now()` (current main); post-fix uses `performance.now()` (this PR).

```console
$ # PRE-FIX (workflow-runtime.ts on Date.now(), i.e. current main) — 3 scenarios:
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/comfy/_proof_wallclock.test.ts \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
[proof] poll round: Date.now() jumped FORWARD +60000ms (simulated NTP skew / manual clock change)
 × forward Date.now jump does NOT cause spurious timeout (monotonic budget)
Error: Comfy workflow did not finish within 10s
 ❯ resolveComfyRemainingMs extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts:486   const remainingMs = deadline - Date.now();
 ❯ waitForComfyHistory extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts:471
 ❯ runComfyWorkflow extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts:806
 ❯ Object.generateImage extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.ts:41
[proof] BACKWARD-jump scenario: completed in 542ms (NOT inflated by the 60s wall-clock rollback)
 ✓ backward Date.now jump does NOT inflate timeout (monotonic budget)
[proof] BOUNDED-EXPIRY scenario (never-compleving workflow, backward -60s jump each poll): STILL POLLING past 6000ms (deadline inflated by wall-clock jump = bug)
 × bounded expiry: never-compleving workflow times out within configured timeoutMs despite backward wall-clock jump (monotonic budget) 6017ms
   → expected true to be false   # hitHardGuard: polling still alive at 3x the 2000ms budget
 Tests  2 failed | 1 passed   # (A) forward=spurious timeout; (C) bounded-expiry=hang past budget; (B) backward short run completes

$ # POST-FIX (this PR, performance.now()) — 3 scenarios:
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/comfy/_proof_wallclock.test.ts \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
[proof] FORWARD-jump scenario: completed in 809ms (bounded by real elapsed time, NOT by the 60s wall-clock jump)
 ✓ forward Date.now jump does NOT cause spurious timeout (monotonic budget)
[proof] BACKWARD-jump scenario: completed in 617ms (NOT inflated by the 60s wall-clock rollback)
 ✓ backward Date.now jump does NOT inflate timeout (monotonic budget)
[proof] BOUNDED-EXPIRY scenario (never-compleving workflow, backward -60s jump each poll): threw in 2488ms
[proof] error message: Comfy workflow did not finish within 2s
 ✓ bounded expiry: never-compleving workflow times out within configured timeoutMs despite backward wall-clock jump (monotonic budget) 2497ms
 Tests  3 passed   # all 3: bounded by real elapsed time, no hang, no spurious timeout
```

The proof drives the production `buildComfyImageGenerationProvider().generateImage()` → `runComfyWorkflow` → `waitForComfyHistory` + `resolveComfyRemainingMs` (the two changed owners) over a real local HTTP server, so `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, its SSRF validation, and the `setTimeout`-based timeout abort signal all execute; only the transport endpoint is a loopback server (no private endpoints, keys, or personal data). The bounded-expiry scenario uses `timeoutMs: 2000` with a server that never returns a completed history, so the only exit is the deadline throwing `"did not finish within 2s"`.

Behavior matrix (observed, all over real HTTP polling):

```text
scenario                                   => pre-fix (Date.now)                              => post-fix (performance.now)
forward jump +60s, workflow completes      => spurious "did not finish within 10s" (FAIL)      => completes ~810ms (PASS)
backward jump -60s, workflow completes     => completes ~540ms (budget inflated, no hang here) => completes ~620ms (PASS)
backward jump -60s, workflow NEVER completes => STILL POLLING past 6000ms (3x budget = hang)   => "did not finish within 2s" at ~2490ms (bounded)
```

Post-fix unit test (full shard, 31/31 pass, including the adapted "caps oversized" case that spies on `performance.now`):

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

What was not tested: `extensions/comfy/music-generation-provider.test.ts` and `extensions/comfy/video-generation-provider.test.ts` could not run in this checkout (the repo's `@openclaw/fs-safe` package does not export its `./watch` subpath here). The music test uses real `timeoutMs: 1000` and asserts `"did not finish within 1s"`; switching to `performance.now()` preserves behavior since both clocks advance past 1000ms identically when not mocked. The proof script is not committed (evidence-only).

Open PR collision check: #117905 (steipete) restructures this region but still uses `Date.now()` for deadline comparison and does not address the cross-clock-domain issue (not a duplicate; rebase risk noted above).
